title: A Beautiful Mind
author: Sylvia Nasar
target_audience: Readers interested in mental health and psychology
Students of history, economics, and mathematics
General readers curious about geniuses and their personal struggles
core_themes: Triumph and tragedy in intellectual life
primary_purpose: To chronicle the extraordinary life and career of mathematician John Nash, exploring his groundbreaking contributions to game theory, his struggle with schizophrenia, and the impact on his personal and professional relationships.

structure_format.narrative_style: Narrative nonfiction; combines biographical storytelling with scientific exposition
structure_format.organization: Chronological, with sections on early life, academic achievements, mental illness, and eventual recognition
features: Interviews with friends, family, and colleagues
Historical context about mathematics and academia
Descriptions of Nash's mathematical ideas for general audiences
In-depth exploration of Nash's mental health journey

key_concepts_lessons: The boundaries between genius and mental illness are often blurred.
Scientific achievement can come at significant personal cost.
Family and community play a crucial role in recovery and support.
Recovery from mental illness is possible, even after long struggles.
Societal stigma around mental health can isolate individuals and hinder understanding.
notable_features: Integrates complex mathematics into an accessible narrative
Personal and scientific facets of Nash's life are explored equally
Basis for the Oscar-winning film of the same name
Relies on extensive interviews and archival material
cultural_historical_context: Published in the late 1990s, the book emerged during increased public interest in mental health and the stories of exceptional minds. It illuminated the achievements of mathematicians and the realities of living with schizophrenia during a period of shifting attitudes toward mental illness.
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed for its depth and sensitivity
Brought awareness to John Nash’s contributions and struggles
Lauded for destigmatizing mental illness through detailed narrative
Inspired a popular feature film, furthering its cultural impact
comparable_titles: The Man Who Knew Infinity: A Life of the Genius Ramanujan by Robert Kanigel
Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman! by Richard P. Feynman
An Unquiet Mind by Kay Redfield Jamison
